# Model and source

Ma, Almasan and Gurkan-Cavusoglu (2022) built an integrated mechanistic
PK / PD model of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) in colon cancer from three sub-models
fitted in sequence by Bayesian MCMC to published mean data:

1. a two-compartment plasma **PK** model with Michaelis-Menten elimination;
2. a **cellular** model of 5-FU in tumour interstitial fluid, uptake into and
   efflux out of tumour cells, anabolism to fluoronucleotides, incorporation
   into RNA and DNA with delayed excision, FdUMP binding to thymidylate
   synthase (TS) in competition with dUMP, the resulting dNTP-pool imbalance
   with salvage feedback, and delayed DNA double-strand-break (DSB) induction;
3. a **tumour growth inhibition (TGI)** model in which the anabolites slow
   logistic growth and the DSB excess over a drug-free baseline turns
   proliferating cells into damaged cells that die after a fixed life span.

The PK and cellular parameters (Table 1) are shared, and the TGI layer was
re-estimated for each of nine xenograft datasets (Table 3 and Table 4). The
library therefore carries **nine model files**, one per TGI model, each with
the full shared PK and cellular layers.

```{r models}
models <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n, ~file,                                             ~cell,                 ~regimen,                                  ~mgkg, ~ii_day, ~ndose, ~dur_day, ~tv0,
  1L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_colon38_weekly_mouse_qsp",   "Colon 38",            "100 mg/kg weekly x 4",                    100,   7,       4L,     45,       125,
  2L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_colon26_daily_mouse_qsp",    "Colon 26",            "50 mg/kg daily x 4",                      50,    1,       4L,     7,        125,
  3L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_ht29_biw_mouse_qsp",         "HT29",                "20 mg/kg twice a week x 3 weeks",         20,    3.5,     6L,     21,       100,
  4L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_ht29_tiw_mouse_qsp",         "HT29",                "20 mg/kg three times a week x 3 weeks",   20,    7 / 3,   9L,     24,       100,
  5L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_sw620_daily_mouse_qsp",      "SW620",               "5 mg/kg daily x 9",                       5,     1,       9L,     9,        56.76,
  6L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_sw620_biw_mouse_qsp",        "SW620",               "20 mg/kg twice a week x 3 weeks",         20,    3.5,     6L,     26,       56.5,
  7L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_sw620_qod_mouse_qsp",        "SW620",               "20 mg/kg every other day x 2 weeks",      20,    2,       7L,     14,       71.3,
  8L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_ls174t_sensitive_mouse_qsp", "LS174T (sensitive)",  "50 mg/kg every other day x 6",            50,    2,       6L,     15,       125,
  9L, "Ma_2022_fluorouracil_ls174t_resistant_mouse_qsp", "LS174T (resistant)",  "50 mg/kg every other day x 6",            50,    2,       6L,     15,       125
)

# readModelDb() returns the model FUNCTION; rxode2::rxode() resolves it to
# the rxUi whose metadata and parameter values are readable.
ui <- lapply(setNames(models$file, models$n), \(f) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(f)))
```

* Citation: Ma C, Almasan A, Gurkan-Cavusoglu E. Computational analysis of
  5-fluorouracil anti-tumor activity in colon cancer using a mechanistic
  pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model. *PLoS Comput Biol*
  2022;18(11):e1010685.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010685>
* Code and MCMC chains deposited by the authors:
  <https://github.com/Chenhui88569/Computational-analysis-of-5-fluorouracil-anti-tumor-activity>
  (Zenodo <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7267874>).

```{r model-table, echo = FALSE}
models |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    "TGI model" = n, "nlmixr2lib model" = file, "Cell line" = cell,
    Regimen = regimen, "Initial tumour volume (mm^3)" = tv0
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "The nine model files contributed by Ma 2022 (Table 3).")
```

## Units and dosing

Time is in **minutes** throughout, as in the paper. The plasma, interstitial
and cellular states are concentrations, so a dose is entered as the plasma
concentration increment it produces. The authors map 100 mg/kg to the first
measured plasma concentration, 92.9936 ug/mL, and scale it linearly with dose
(46.5 ug/mL at 50 mg/kg, 18.6 ug/mL at 20 mg/kg); this vignette uses
`0.929936 * dose (mg/kg)`. The `delay()` terms need a dense ODE solver and the
interstitial-fluid exchange is fast (k03 = 136/min), so every solve below uses
`method = "dop853"` with a large `maxsteps`.

```{r helpers}
mgkg_to_conc <- function(mgkg) 0.929936306 * mgkg

# One treated or control animal on a regimen. Observation rows use the
# `anabolites` state as their compartment: it is one of the model's declared
# endpoints, and every other output is returned on the same rows.
sim_regimen <- function(file, mgkg, ii_day, ndose, tv0, times, params = NULL) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(times)
  if (mgkg > 0 && ndose > 1) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(
      amt = mgkg_to_conc(mgkg), cmt = "central",
      ii = ii_day * 1440, addl = ndose - 1
    ) |> rxode2::et(times)
  } else if (mgkg > 0) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = mgkg_to_conc(mgkg), cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(times)
  }
  ev <- as.data.frame(ev)
  ev$TUM_VOL <- tv0
  ev$cmt[ev$evid == 0] <- "anabolites"
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    readModelDb(file), ev,
    params = params, method = "dop853", maxsteps = 1e7,
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}
```

# Population

There are no individual animals: every sub-model was fitted to group means
taken from the literature (Ma 2022 Table 2 for the PK and cellular data,
Table 3 for the tumour-volume data), so the model has no between-animal
variability and every simulation below is deterministic.

* **PK** -- C57BL/6 mice bearing Colon 38 tumours, 100 mg/kg intraperitoneal.
* **Cellular layer** -- intracellular 5-FU and anabolites in C57BL/6 mice with
  C38 tumours (115 mg/kg); FU-RNA and FU-DNA in BALB/c mice with Colon 26-B
  tumours (80 mg/kg); TS-FdUMP complex and total TS in Wistar rats with
  dimethylhydrazine-induced colon carcinoma (100 mg/kg); dUMP in BALB/c mice
  with colon tumour 06/A (80 mg/kg); dNTP pools in L5178 lymphoma cells in
  vitro (1 uM); DSBs in OCI-AML2 leukaemia cells in vitro (3 umol/L).
* **TGI layer** -- nine published xenograft or syngeneic colon-tumour
  datasets (Colon 38, Colon 26, HT29, SW620 and 5-FU-sensitive and -resistant
  LS174T), normalised to the starting tumour volume.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Model variable / parameter | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plasma PK (Eqs 1-3) | `central`, `peripheral1`; `lvmax`, `lkm`, `lq`, `lvc`, `lvp` | Methods 'PK model'; Table 1 'PK model' |
| Interstitial 5-FU, uptake, efflux, anabolism (Eqs 4-6) | `isf`, `intracellular`, `anabolites`; `q_isf`, `vmax_influx`, `km_influx`, `vmax_efflux`, `km_efflux`, `k03`, `vmax_anab`, `km_anab` | Eqs 4-6; Table 1 |
| FU-RNA, FU-DNA with delayed excision (Eqs 7-8) | `fu_rna`, `fu_dna`; `k65`, `k56`, `k06`, `gamma_rna`, `vmax_dna_in`, `km_dna_in`, `vmax_dna_out`, `km_dna_out`, `k07`, `gamma_dna`, `td_rna`, `td_dna` | Eqs 7-8; Table 1 |
| TS-FdUMP complex, total TS, TS-dUMP, dUMP (Eqs 9-15) | `ts_fdump`, `dump`; `k95`, `k59`, `k09`, `kd_dump`, `g0_dump`, `kcat`, `k08`, `alpha_ts`, `kd_ts`, `ts0` | Eqs 9-15; Table 1 |
| dNTP-pool imbalance and salvage (Eqs 17-19) | `nucp`, `salvage`; `k1_dntp` ... `k10_dntp`, `kb_dntp`, `ka_dntp`, `gamma_dntp` | Eqs 17-19; Table 1 |
| DSB induction and drug-free baseline (Eqs 20-22) | `dsb`, `dsb_baseline`; `vmax_dntp`, `km_dntp`, `vmax_hr`, `km_hr`, `ki_hr`, `k0_dsb`, `gamma_dsb`, `td_dsb` | Eqs 20-22; Table 1; `km_dntp` from the deposited MCMC chain |
| TGI (Eqs 23-28) | `cycling_cells`, `damaged_cells1`, `tumor_vol`; `td_tv`, `ic50`, `emax_damage`, `ec50_damage`, `lambda_g`, `pmax`, `lambda_d`, `gamma_tv` | Eqs 23-28; Table 4 (per model) |
| Initial dUMP 3.878 and DSB 42.755 pmol/mg / thousand breaks | `dump(0)`, `dsb(0)`, `dsb_baseline(0)` | first (0 h) literature data points, as coded in the deposit |
| Initial tumour volume | `TUM_VOL` covariate | deposited code (`CollectDataIntoNestedStructure.m`) |
| Residual SDs (sqrt of the reported variances) | `addSd`, `addSd_<endpoint>` | Table 1 and Table 4; PK and FU-RNA variances from the deposited MCMC chains |
| Dose-to-concentration mapping | `0.929936 * mg/kg` | deposited code |

# Single 100 mg/kg dose: PK and cellular layers (Figures 2 and 3)

The PK and cellular parameters were fitted to a single intraperitoneal dose of
100 mg/kg (115 mg/kg and 80 mg/kg for some cellular data sets). The
literature means the authors fitted are embedded in their deposited code and
are overlaid here.

```{r single-dose}
t_sd <- sort(unique(c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 45, seq(60, 4320, by = 30))))
sd1 <- sim_regimen(models$file[1], 100, 7, 1L, 125, t_sd) |>
  mutate(pct_free_ts = 100 * ts_free / ts_total)

obs_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(var = "Plasma 5-FU (ug/mL)", time = c(0, 10, 20, 30, 60, 90, 120, 240),
                 value = c(92.99, 70.25, 67.09, 48.33, 26.12, 11.39, 5.574, 1.753)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "Intracellular 5-FU (pmol/mg)", time = c(15, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 105, 120),
                 value = c(159.96, 133.32, 110.81, 39.86, 86.68, 62.38, 11.88, 46.23, 6.244, 8.477)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "Anabolites (pmol/mg)", time = c(15, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 105, 120),
                 value = c(29.34, 50.22, 42.82, 49.19, 43.57, 75.71, 67.86, 63.12, 73.78, 61.79)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "FU-RNA (pmol/mg)", time = c(2, 8, 24, 48, 72) * 60,
                 value = c(9.617, 6.488, 9.155, 2.366, 2.881) * 2),
  tibble::tibble(var = "FU-DNA (pmol/mg)", time = c(2, 8, 24, 48, 72) * 60,
                 value = c(15.53, 13.61, 15.76, 9.854, 14.43) * 2e-4),
  tibble::tibble(var = "TS-FdUMP complex (pmol/mg)", time = c(2, 6, 24, 32, 48) * 60,
                 value = c(0.0355, 0.0307, 0.0272, 0.0217, 0.0180)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "dUMP (pmol/mg)", time = c(3, 12, 24, 48) * 60,
                 value = c(5.770, 4.974, 5.552, 3.528)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "dNTP-pool imbalance", time = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12) * 60,
                 value = c(0.1532, 0.7109, 0.7337, 0.8817, 1.1337, 0.8240, 0.7070, 0.3747)),
  tibble::tibble(var = "DSB (thousands)", time = c(8, 24, 32, 48, 64, 72) * 60,
                 value = c(74.76, 74.28, 113.82, 226.81, 189.08, 132.25))
)

sim_sd <- sd1 |>
  transmute(
    time,
    "Plasma 5-FU (ug/mL)" = Cc,
    "Intracellular 5-FU (pmol/mg)" = intracellular,
    "Anabolites (pmol/mg)" = anabolites,
    "FU-RNA (pmol/mg)" = fu_rna,
    "FU-DNA (pmol/mg)" = fu_dna,
    "TS-FdUMP complex (pmol/mg)" = ts_fdump,
    "dUMP (pmol/mg)" = dump,
    "dNTP-pool imbalance" = nucp,
    "DSB (thousands)" = dsb
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "var")
```

```{r fig-single-dose, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Replicates Figures 2 and 3 of Ma 2022: the shared PK and cellular layers after a single 100 mg/kg dose (line) against the literature means the authors fitted (points). The DSB data extend to 72 h, so the x-axis is cut at 3 days."}
ggplot(sim_sd, aes(time / 60, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = obs_sd, colour = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The free-TS fraction falls to its minimum about 5 h after the dose and dUMP
peaks at the same time, as described in the Results ('Cellular model'). The
DSB count rises through the first hours toward the drug-free baseline and
only climbs above it after the 1.8-day delay `Td,DSB`.

```{r single-dose-checks}
peak_dump_h <- sd1$time[which.max(sd1$dump)] / 60
min_free_h <- sd1$time[which.min(sd1$pct_free_ts)] / 60
stopifnot(
  abs(peak_dump_h - min_free_h) < 1.5,
  peak_dump_h > 3, peak_dump_h < 8
)
c(dUMP_peak_h = peak_dump_h, free_TS_minimum_h = min_free_h)
```

## Plasma NCA

Ma 2022 reports no NCA for 5-FU. The table compares the PKNCA summary of the
simulated plasma profile with that of the literature means the PK model was
fitted to (Table 2, reference 65).

```{r pknca}
pk_sim <- sd1 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 240) |>
  transmute(id = 1L, treatment = "100 mg/kg", time, Cc)
pk_obs <- obs_sd |>
  filter(var == "Plasma 5-FU (ug/mL)") |>
  transmute(id = 1L, treatment = "100 mg/kg", time, Cc = value)
dose_df <- tibble::tibble(id = 1L, treatment = "100 mg/kg", time = 0, amt = mgkg_to_conc(100))

nca_fun <- function(conc_df) {
  conc <- PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc, dose, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_sim <- nca_fun(pk_sim)
nca_obs <- nca_fun(pk_obs)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(nca_sim, nca_obs, by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast", "half.life"))
```

```{r pknca-check}
auc_ratio <- as.data.frame(nca_sim) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |> pull(PPORRES) /
  (as.data.frame(nca_obs) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |> pull(PPORRES))
stopifnot(abs(auc_ratio - 1) < 0.15)
auc_ratio
```

# Reproducing the authors' multi-dose drivers

The authors pre-computed the anabolite and DSB time courses that drive each
TGI fit and deposited them with their code. Their multi-dose simulation code
enters the two excision delays `Td,RNA` and `Td,DNA` in **minutes** (0.396 and
4.360 min), whereas Table 1 reports them in **days** and their single-dose
fitting code converts days to minutes. The library models carry the Table 1
values in days. Overriding the two delays with the deposit's minute values
reproduces the deposited time courses, which tests every other equation of
the PK, cellular, dNTP and DSB layers against the authors' own numbers.

```{r deposit-check}
deposit_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n, ~time,      ~a5,       ~dsb,
  1L, 62.0530,    58.415,    69.323,
  1L, 123.6431,   79.014,    73.709,
  1L, 278.9780,   87.803,    74.707,
  1L, 606.4480,   82.461,    74.724,
  1L, 1425.1276,  66.774,    74.724,
  1L, 2721.6811,  43.016,    164.59,
  1L, 4425.2147,  13.699,    127.96,
  1L, 7316.3939,  NA,        107.81,
  5L, 11629.6815, 3.0782,    90.682,
  8L, 1454.5650,  24.781,    74.724,
  8L, 3001.9917,  43.143,    166.46,
  8L, 14643.3688, 50.280,    145.58
)
deposit_lags <- c(td_rna = 0.39587 / 1440, td_dna = 4.35978 / 1440)

deposit_cmp <- deposit_ref |>
  group_by(n) |>
  group_modify(\(d, k) {
    m <- models[models$n == k$n, ]
    s <- sim_regimen(m$file, m$mgkg, m$ii_day, m$ndose, m$tv0,
      sort(unique(c(0, d$time))), params = deposit_lags)
    s <- s[match(d$time, s$time), ]
    mutate(d, a5_sim = s$anabolites, dsb_sim = s$dsb)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    pct_a5 = 100 * (a5_sim - a5) / a5,
    pct_dsb = 100 * (dsb_sim - dsb) / dsb
  )

deposit_cmp |>
  mutate(across(c(a5_sim, dsb_sim, pct_a5, pct_dsb), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "TGI model" = n, "Time (min)" = time,
    "Anabolites, deposit" = a5, "Anabolites, model" = a5_sim, "Anabolites diff (%)" = pct_a5,
    "DSB, deposit" = dsb, "DSB, model" = dsb_sim, "DSB diff (%)" = pct_dsb
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Deposited anabolite and DSB time courses versus the library model with the deposit's minute-valued excision delays.")
```

Both sides are deterministic solves of the same equations, so the remaining
differences are the rounding of the Table 1 values (printed to three or four
significant figures) and solver error.

```{r deposit-check-assert}
stopifnot(
  max(abs(deposit_cmp$pct_a5), na.rm = TRUE) < 3,
  max(abs(deposit_cmp$pct_dsb)) < 3
)
```

The two readings of the delays differ only in how long the excision of
FU-RNA and FU-DNA runs at its pre-dose rate, so they diverge after a dose:

```{r delay-units}
sd_dep <- sim_regimen(models$file[1], 100, 7, 1L, 125, t_sd, params = deposit_lags)
delay_units <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("Peak anabolites (pmol/mg)", "Peak DSB (thousands)"),
  table1_days = c(max(sd1$anabolites), max(sd1$dsb)),
  deposit_minutes = c(max(sd_dep$anabolites), max(sd_dep$dsb))
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (table1_days - deposit_minutes) / deposit_minutes)
delay_units |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Quantity = quantity, "Table 1 delays (days)" = table1_days,
    "Deposit delays (minutes)" = deposit_minutes, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Single 100 mg/kg dose: effect of the excision-delay units.")
```

With the delays in days, the delayed-excision factor stays at its pre-dose
value for longer, so more fluoronucleotide returns from RNA to the anabolite
pool. The tumour-volume predictions are insensitive to this because the
anabolites act through `A5^0.2` (the Table 5 comparison below shows the
first-week exposure metrics agree to a few per cent).

The literature tumour volumes (normalised to the first measurement) are the
values the authors digitised into their deposit. TGI model 2 is simulated only
through day 3: the published cellular layer becomes singular during the fourth
daily 50 mg/kg dose (see 'Assumptions and deviations').

```{r tgi-sim}
tgi_end_day <- ifelse(models$n == 2L, 3, models$dur_day)
tgi_ndose <- ifelse(models$n == 2L, 3L, models$ndose)

tgi_sim <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(models)), \(i) {
  m <- models[i, ]
  end_min <- tgi_end_day[i] * 1440
  obs_t <- tgi_obs$time_min[tgi_obs$model == m$n]
  times <- sort(unique(c(0, seq(0, 7 * 1440, by = 30), seq(0, end_min, by = 360),
    obs_t[obs_t <= end_min])))
  times <- times[times <= end_min]
  sim_regimen(m$file, m$mgkg, m$ii_day, tgi_ndose[i], m$tv0, times) |>
    mutate(n = m$n, rtv = tumor_vol / (m$tv0 / 1000))
}) |> bind_rows()

# The drug-free arm reduces to logistic growth with net rate lambda_g -
# lambda_d and ceiling Pmax * (1 - lambda_d / lambda_g); see the identity
# check below.
control_closed <- function(time, n, tv0) {
  th <- ui[[as.character(n)]]$theta
  p0 <- tv0 / 1000
  r <- th[["lambda_g"]] - th[["lambda_d"]]
  k <- th[["pmax"]] * (1 - th[["lambda_d"]] / th[["lambda_g"]])
  k / (1 + (k / p0 - 1) * exp(-r * time)) / p0
}
tgi_ctl <- models |>
  group_by(n) |>
  reframe(time = seq(0, dur_day * 1440, by = 360), rtv = control_closed(time, n, tv0))
```

```{r fig-tgi, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Ma 2022: relative tumour volume of the treated (blue) and drug-free control (red) groups for the nine TGI models; points are the literature data the authors fitted."}
short_reg <- c("100 mg/kg qw x4", "50 mg/kg qd x4", "20 mg/kg biw x3 wk", "20 mg/kg tiw x3 wk",
  "5 mg/kg qd x9", "20 mg/kg biw x3 wk", "20 mg/kg q2d x2 wk", "50 mg/kg q2d x6", "50 mg/kg q2d x6")
panel_lab <- setNames(paste0("(", models$n, ") ", models$cell, "\n", short_reg), models$n)
obs_long <- tgi_obs |>
  pivot_longer(c(rtv_treated, rtv_control), names_to = "arm", values_to = "rtv") |>
  filter(!is.na(rtv)) |>
  mutate(arm = ifelse(arm == "rtv_treated", "treated", "control"), n = model)
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = tgi_sim, aes(time / 1440, rtv, colour = "treated")) +
  geom_line(data = tgi_ctl, aes(time / 1440, rtv, colour = "control"), linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(data = obs_long, aes(time_min / 1440, rtv, colour = arm, shape = arm)) +
  facet_wrap(~n, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(n = panel_lab)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(treated = "steelblue", control = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Relative tumour volume", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r tgi-fit}
tgi_fit <- tgi_obs |>
  rename(n = model) |>
  inner_join(tgi_sim |> select(n, time, rtv), by = c("n", "time_min" = "time")) |>
  group_by(n) |>
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(),
    median_abs_log_ratio = median(abs(log(rtv / rtv_treated))),
    final_sim = last(rtv), final_obs = last(rtv_treated)
  )
tgi_fit |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "TGI model" = n, "Treated data points" = n_obs,
    "Median |log(sim/obs)|" = median_abs_log_ratio,
    "Final simulated" = final_sim, "Final observed" = final_obs
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Treated-group relative tumour volume, model versus literature data.")
```

The treated-group fits match the quality shown in Figure 4, including the
authors' own remarks: model 4 (HT29, three times weekly), which reuses the
model 3 efficacy parameters, fits only moderately, and model 1 over-predicts
the Colon 38 tumours between weeks 2 and 6.

```{r tgi-fit-assert}
stopifnot(
  median(tgi_fit$median_abs_log_ratio) < 0.15,
  max(tgi_fit$median_abs_log_ratio) < 0.4
)
```

## Drug-free arm identity

With no dose the anabolites and the DSB excess stay at zero, so Eq 23
reduces to `dP/dt = lambda_g P (1 - P/Pmax) - lambda_d P` with a closed-form
logistic solution. Solving the model for an untreated TGI model 7 animal
checks the TGI code path against it.

```{r control-identity}
m7 <- models[models$n == 7L, ]
ctl7 <- sim_regimen(m7$file, 0, 1, 1L, m7$tv0, seq(0, m7$dur_day * 1440, by = 720)) |>
  mutate(closed = control_closed(time, 7L, m7$tv0), rtv = tumor_vol / (m7$tv0 / 1000))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(ctl7$rtv - ctl7$closed) / ctl7$closed) < 1e-4,
  all(ctl7$anabolites == 0), all(ctl7$damaged_cells1 == 0)
)
max(abs(ctl7$rtv - ctl7$closed) / ctl7$closed)
```

# Exposure metrics over the first week (Table 5)

Table 5 integrates, over the first week of each regimen, the anabolite
amount (`AUC_a`), the relative DSB excess (`AUC_DSB`) and the two effect
functions `Ea(t)` and `EDSB(t)` (`AUC_e,a`, `AUC_e,DSB`), all with time in
days. The authors' values come from their minute-delay drivers; the library
values use the Table 1 delays in days. Model 2 is omitted because its
published driver is singular after day 3.

```{r table5}
trapz <- function(x, y) sum(diff(x) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
table5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~n, ~auc_ea, ~auc_edsb, ~auc_a,   ~auc_dsb,
  1L, 4.7900,  1.2874,    162.4190, 2.8343,
  3L, 4.9206,  0.3889,    17.2567,  0.9044,
  4L, 3.8823,  0.4494,    25.8850,  1.1920,
  5L, 5.0412,  1.7674,    4.2039,   0.6292,
  6L, 4.9206,  0.3895,    17.2567,  0.9044,
  7L, 3.1336,  0.4631,    34.5052,  1.3578,
  8L, 3.9429,  0.7832,    194.0453, 3.6296,
  9L, 3.8757,  2.4385,    194.0453, 3.6296
)
week <- tgi_sim |>
  filter(n %in% table5$n, time <= 7 * 1440) |>
  group_by(n) |>
  summarise(
    sim_auc_ea = trapz(time / 1440, e_a),
    sim_auc_edsb = trapz(time / 1440, e_dsb),
    sim_auc_a = trapz(time / 1440, anabolites),
    sim_auc_dsb = trapz(time / 1440, dsb_deviation)
  ) |>
  inner_join(table5, by = "n")
```

```{r table5-tidy}
cmp5 <- week |>
  transmute(
    n,
    AUC_e_a = 100 * (sim_auc_ea - auc_ea) / auc_ea,
    AUC_e_DSB = 100 * (sim_auc_edsb - auc_edsb) / auc_edsb,
    AUC_a = 100 * (sim_auc_a - auc_a) / auc_a,
    AUC_DSB = 100 * (sim_auc_dsb - auc_dsb) / auc_dsb
  )
week |>
  transmute(
    n,
    "AUC_e,a (paper / model)" = paste(signif(auc_ea, 4), signif(sim_auc_ea, 4), sep = " / "),
    "AUC_e,DSB (paper / model)" = paste(signif(auc_edsb, 4), signif(sim_auc_edsb, 4), sep = " / "),
    "AUC_a (paper / model)" = paste(signif(auc_a, 4), signif(sim_auc_a, 4), sep = " / "),
    "AUC_DSB (paper / model)" = paste(signif(auc_dsb, 4), signif(sim_auc_dsb, 4), sep = " / ")
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("TGI model" = n) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ma 2022 Table 5 versus the library models (first week, time in days).")
```

```{r table5-assert}
cmp5
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cmp5$AUC_a)) < 5,
  max(abs(cmp5$AUC_DSB)) < 5,
  max(abs(cmp5$AUC_e_a)) < 5,
  max(abs(cmp5$AUC_e_DSB)) < 20
)
```

The anabolite and DSB exposures agree within a few per cent despite the
different delay units. `AUC_e,DSB` runs 4-12% below Table 5 for a reason
outside the model: the authors align their control DSB curve to the treated
time grid by interpolation, which leaves a relative DSB excess of up to
1.3e-3 during the first 1.8 days, when the true excess is exactly zero.
`EDSB` raises that excess to the power 0.2, so the artefact adds about 0.033
to every `AUC_e,DSB` in Table 5 (recomputing Table 5 from the deposited time
courses reproduces the printed values, and the first 1.8 days contribute
0.0333 for both model 3 and model 8). Without it the library values agree
to within about 2%.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Excision delays in days.** Table 1 lists `Td,RNA = 0.396` and
  `Td,DNA = 4.360` in days, and the authors' single-dose fitting code
  converts them from days to minutes; their multi-dose code (which generated
  the TGI drivers behind Table 4 and Figure 4) uses the same numbers as
  minutes. The library follows Table 1. The deposit's behaviour is recovered
  with `params = c(td_rna = 0.39587 / 1440, td_dna = 4.35978 / 1440)`, as
  shown above; tumour-volume predictions differ by well under 1%.
* **Values not printed in the paper.** `K_dNTP` appears in Eq 21 but not in
  Table 1, and the residual variances of plasma 5-FU and FU-RNA are not
  printed. All three are the posterior means of the authors' deposited MCMC
  chains (`Para_dNTP_DSB_col_2.mat`, `Para_PK_col.mat`,
  `Para_Cellular_col.mat`) over the authors' own burn-in, which reproduces
  every printed Table 1 value: `K_dNTP = 151.918`, plasma variance 52.112
  (ug/mL)^2, FU-RNA variance 4.991 (pmol/mg)^2. The initial dUMP (3.878
  pmol/mg) and DSB (42.755 thousand) levels and the initial tumour volumes
  of the nine datasets are also taken from the deposited code.
* **Total TS resets at each dose.** Eq 10 is a function of `t`; the
  authors restart the integration clock at every dose, so `t` is the time
  since the most recent dose (`tad()`). An undosed animal uses the time since
  the start of the simulation, as the authors' control runs do.
* **Model 2 is singular after its third dose.** Under daily 50 mg/kg the
  TS-FdUMP complex comes to exceed the total TS of Eq 10 after the fourth
  dose, so the free TS of Eq 11 turns negative. Once it falls below
  `-K_dUMP * k08 / kcat` (about -0.04 pmol/mg) the dUMP equation has a
  positive linear coefficient and grows exponentially toward the pole of
  Eq 13 at `TSf = -K_dUMP`; the solver stops shortly after 4500 min. The
  authors' deposited model 2 driver is complex-valued over the same window.
  The model is encoded as published; only model 2's regimen reaches this
  regime among the nine.
* **Fractional powers guarded at zero.** `(1 - TSf/TStotal)^gamma_dNTP`,
  `Nucp(t - Td,DSB)^gamma_DSB`, `A5^gamma_Tv` and the relative DSB excess are
  evaluated on `max(x, 0)`. These quantities are non-negative in exact
  arithmetic; the guard only stops round-off below zero from producing `NaN`
  (the authors' MATLAB code returns complex numbers there and keeps the real
  part).
* **Doses as plasma-concentration increments.** The PK states are
  concentrations (Table 1 gives `Vmax` in ug/mL/min and `Km` in ug/mL), and the
  authors start each dose at the first measured plasma concentration (92.9936
  ug/mL for 100 mg/kg), scaled linearly with dose.
* **Units printed in Table 1.** `k06` and `k07` (min^-1 in Table 1) multiply
  an amount inside `(1 + k * A)^gamma` and therefore carry mg/pmol; `k95`
  multiplies TS and A5 and carries mg/pmol/min; `G0` is printed as mg/min but
  is a zero-order synthesis rate in pmol/mg/min; the dNTP-layer constants are
  printed as unitless although `k1`, `k3`, `k5`, `k9` and `k10` act as rates per
  minute. The parameter labels state the dimensionally consistent unit.
* **Control and treated residual variances.** Table 4 reports separate
  noise variances for the control and treated tumour volumes. Both arms use
  the same equations, so the model exposes the tumour volume twice:
  `tumor_vol` (treated variance) and `tumor_vol_control` (control variance).
* **Plasma PK with no drug loss to the tumour.** Eq 4 adds `Q31 * Cp` to the
  interstitial fluid without removing it from plasma, as published.
